searchText: thanks for the prompt reply, I think I was a bit confused with the fact that you can't forward sync from before the blob availability window and somehow assumed that if you were to spin up a new node this would affect syncing from genesis we can't guarantee that the blobs outside the availability window would be available over p2p. so if we genesis sync, we have to assume that they were available at that time right, so this applies to blobs only though, correct? we can still fetch all the blocks In practice probably, but `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#configuration) is still only 5 months. even pre-Dencun, in theory genesis sync isn't really "supported", right now got it thanks!! hey I was looking at blob transactions here from dencun - https://blobscan.com/txs * I thought per EIP-4844 the max blob size is 125kb not 128kb? * is it possible to submit a blob with less than the max size? For instance if I was a rollup, could I submit a blob with 25kb sie? I think all blobs are padded with zeros so that they are always 128kb Is this a requirement for blobs to be submitted then? Or is this just for testnet purposes https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4844 defines a blob as `ByteVector[BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT * FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB]` i.e. 32 * 4096 = 131072 bytes. This is 128KiB (kibibits, the base 2 version). https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/deneb/polynomial-commitments.md#constants similarly defines `BYTES_PER_BLOB` as `uint64(BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT * FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB)` which also is 131,072 bytes for the same reason.

excerpts.author: pawandhananjay
excerpts.content: we can't  guarantee that the blobs outside the availability window would be available over p2p. so if we genesis sync, we have to assume that they were available at that time

excerpts.author: marianna_metrika
excerpts.content: right, so this applies to blobs only though, correct? we can still fetch all the blocks

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: In practice probably, but `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#configuration) is still only 5 months.

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: even pre-Dencun, in theory genesis sync isn't really "supported", right now

hey I was looking at blob transactions here from dencun - https://blobscan.com/txs

* I thought per EIP-4844 the max blob size is 125kb not 128kb?
* is it possible to submit a blob with less than the max size? For instance if I was a rollup, could I submit a blob with 25kb sie?

excerpts.author: marianna_metrika
excerpts.content: I think all blobs are padded with zeros so that they are always 128kb

excerpts.author: 0xevan
excerpts.content: Is this a requirement for blobs to be submitted then? Or is this just for testnet purposes

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4844 defines a blob as `ByteVector[BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT * FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB]` i.e. 32 * 4096 = 131072 bytes. This is 128KiB (kibibits, the base 2 version). https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/deneb/polynomial-commitments.md#constants similarly defines `BYTES_PER_BLOB` as `uint64(BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT * FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB)` which also is 131,072 bytes for the same reason.
